description: ResilienceBench is published by the inormis repository maintainer as an open benchmark for rare failures in critical infrastructure. It contains YAML scenario specifications, synthetic trace generation, baseline failure detectors, evaluation scripts and CSV and HTML reports. The documented scenarios include latency spikes, garbage-collection slowdown, network partition, silent corruption, node crashes and transport SCADA signal loss. Example system profiles represent three or four nodes, and the listed scenarios last 900 to 1,800 seconds. These are synthetic configurations, with no measured geographic coverage or empirical observation period. Python source and usage instructions are public on GitHub under Apache-2.0 and are free to use. The command-line workflow generates traces, applies detectors and measures tail latency, error budgets and detection precision and recall. It can support comparative resilience experiments for cloud services and transport control communications. Limitations are the small synthetic profiles and chaos-tool integrations described as dry-run generators. The review did not execute the benchmark or verify claimed statistical properties. As a catalogue comparison, it complements CloudSim (platform-cloudsim): ResilienceBench focuses on trace generation and failure detection, not general data-centre resource allocation.
name: ResilienceBench
notes: G7 G7-0005. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-27; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability. Synthetic benchmark, not empirical outage observations. Chaos-tool integrations are documented as dry-run generators. Performance and compliance claims were not independently tested.
